conceptTag: Design a bonus nobody can game
readerTitle: Design a bonus your team can't game
caseNote: 가상 시뮬레이션: 생활용품 소매 체인 안의 물류창고 팀. 하나의 이야기로 이어지는 판단 4개. softwareNote로 고객지원 팀 사례 추가.
insight: 보너스는 숫자 하나가 아니라 작은 시스템이다. 사람들은 돈까지 가는 가장 짧은 길을 찾는다. 설계자의 일은 그 지름길이 원하는 행동과 같아지도록 만드는 것이다.
misconception: 측정하기 쉬운 핵심 지표 하나에 돈을 걸면 사람들이 그 지표만큼 일을 더 잘하게 된다.

sources.text: 경영·시스템 사고의 표준 개념 (굿하트의 법칙, 지연, 부분 최적화, 의도치 않은 결과)
모든 상황과 인물은 설명용 가상 사례

factChecks.note: 모든 상황은 가상이며 실제 수치나 연구 결과를 인용하지 않았습니다. '매장이 1~2주 뒤 오류를 확인한다'는 설정은 설명용 가정입니다.
takeaway의 판단-개념 연결(1 굿하트의 법칙, 2 지연, 3 부분 최적화, 4 의도치 않은 결과)이 THK-06 유닛 레슨 내용과 맞는지 확인하세요. 특히 THK-06-09(Wells Fargo)와 사례가 겹치지 않는지 확인이 필요합니다.
다음 레슨 예고는 THK-07-01(Define the problem first) 기준으로 적었습니다. 실제 학습 경로의 다음 레슨에 맞게 수정하세요.

cards.title: Design a bonus your team can't game
body: You run the warehouse team that fills orders for a home-goods retailer's 30 stores. Orders go out too slowly, and your boss gives you a budget for a monthly team bonus.
Every bonus is a small system. People will find the shortest path to the money. Your job is to make that shortest path the one you actually want. Four decisions ahead.

image.label: Warehouse aisle with a bonus envelope at the end of a maze of shelves
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 창고 선반이 미로처럼 놓여 있고, 미로 끝에 'Bonus' 봉투. 직원 캐릭터 하나가 선반 사이 틈으로 지름길을 내려는 모습. 실제 기업 로고나 상표 없음.

cards.title: What should the bonus count?
body: Your first draft pays for **cases picked per hour**. It's easy to count, and it's already on the dashboard.
Before you launch, what do you do?

options.text: Launch it. Speed is the problem you were asked to fix
options.feedback: Speed jumps in week one. So do wrong items and crushed boxes, because nothing in the bonus says *correct*.

options.text: Count only cases that reach the store correct and undamaged
options.feedback: Speed still pays, but only when it's real. Rushing stops paying, so careful speed becomes the shortest path.

options.text: Switch to accuracy only, since errors are costly
options.feedback: Errors fall, but the slowest, most careful picker earns the most. Orders get slower, the problem you started with.

cards.title: When do you pay?
body: Say you chose to count only correct cases.
Stores find errors when they unpack, often a week or two after the truck arrives. The truth about each pick shows up late.

options.text: Pay weekly, based on cases scanned at the dock
options.feedback: Fast and motivating, but you pay for errors nobody has found yet. The bonus rewards what looks right at the dock.

options.text: Pay monthly, after the stores' error reports close
options.feedback: A short wait, but the money matches what really happened. People can still see the link to their work.

options.text: Pay quarterly, once everything is fully counted
options.feedback: Very accurate, but three months is a long time. The link between today's effort and the payout fades.

cards.title: The easy orders vanish first.
body: Say you pay monthly, after store reports. In week three, day-shift scores climb.
Pickers are grabbing quick, single-item orders. Big mixed orders pile up for the night shift, and some stores get deliveries a day late.

image.label: Small orders cleared, big orders stacked for the night shift
image.brief: 창고 바닥을 위에서 본 장면. 낮 시간 쪽은 작은 상자들이 깨끗이 비워져 있고, 밤 시간 쪽에는 큰 혼합 주문 팔레트가 높게 쌓여 있음. 해와 달 아이콘으로 교대조 구분. 로고 없음.

options.text: Pay one shared pool per shift, based on all orders out correct and on time
options.feedback: Hard orders become everyone's problem, and fast pickers start helping on big ones. The cost: some top pickers may feel they carry others, so keep teams small enough to see each other's work.

options.text: Stop letting people choose: assign orders strictly in queue
options.feedback: Cherry-picking stops, but each person still chases a personal number. Expect the next shortcut soon.

options.text: Give extra points for hard orders
options.feedback: Now people argue about which orders count as hard. The points table becomes the new game.

cards.title: Someone stayed quiet.
body: Say you chose the shared pool. In month two, store complaints drop.
Then a loader admits he saw a wrong pallet go out and said nothing. Reporting it would have cost the whole shift its bonus.

options.text: Errors caught before the truck leaves cost nothing. Only errors stores find count
options.feedback: People now hunt for mistakes instead of hiding them. Your error count may rise at first, because you finally see the real ones.

options.text: Add surprise audits and a penalty for hidden errors
options.feedback: You'll catch some hiding. But fear grows, and people get better at hiding.

options.text: Drop accuracy from the bonus to end the pressure
options.feedback: The silence ends, but so does the reason to pick carefully. You're back at decision one.

cards.title: Four pieces that close each other's shortcuts.
body: Here is the bonus you ended up with:
list: **Count:** correct cases, not just fast ones
**Timing:** pay after the stores confirm what arrived
**Honesty:** mistakes caught before the truck leaves cost nothing
cards.callout: No piece is clever alone. Each one blocks a shortcut the others left open.
cards.softwareNote: A support team paid per ticket closed will close tickets fast and watch them reopen. Count tickets that stay closed for a week, pool by team, and don't punish bugs people flag themselves.

cards.title: No bonus is fully ungameable.
body: People are smarter than any formula. Expect a new shortcut every few months, and treat it as information about your design, not as betrayal.
Keep the rules simple enough to explain in one breath, and keep a manager's judgment for what the numbers miss. The bigger the share of pay riding on the number, the harder people will push on it.

cards.title: Design for the shortest path to the money.
body: Each decision you made used one idea from this unit:
list: Decision 1 · **Goodhart's law:** a single measure that becomes a target gets gamed, so pair it with what you care about
Decision 2 · **Delays:** pay when the truth arrives, not before
Decision 3 · **Local wins, global losses:** reward the whole flow, not each piece
Decision 4 · **Unintended consequences:** check what your rule teaches people to hide
cards.callout: **Try it today:** pick one target or bonus you've set. Write down the fastest way someone could hit it without helping the business.
